facts.text: My hands and feet look bluish.
I get Raynaud's: my fingers change colour.

facts.item: how the bluish colour and Raynaud's have changed
facts.text: Both have been getting worse over the past month.
I get short of breath when I exert myself.
I've been feeling nauseous.
I have burning, tingling sensations in my legs.

facts.item: how long the breathlessness, nausea and leg burning have lasted
facts.text: They've come on over the past month.
I've lost 7 to 8 kg.
I keep getting lower back pain.
My periods have been coming too often.

facts.item: how long the weight loss, back pain and period changes have lasted
facts.text: These have been going on over the past 6 months.
The skin on my upper body, arms and legs has become darker.
My skin is red.
The skin on my thighs and legs looks mottled, like a net pattern.
Parts of my skin have become thick and tight.

facts.item: slipped discs in the lower back
facts.text: I've had several slipped discs in my lower back that were treated with surgery.
Two years ago I was diagnosed with 'triple-negative' essential thrombocythemia, where the body makes too many platelets.
I take aspirin for the platelet condition.
I take anagrelide for the platelet condition.
I have blood taken off (phlebotomy) from time to time for the platelet condition.
I was referred to be checked for possible systemic sclerosis.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: Hyperpigmentation of the upper trunk and limbs; erythroderma; acrocyanosis; Raynaud phenomenon; leukonychia; livedo reticularis on the thighs and legs; sclerodermoid changes; digital clubbing.

findings.name: nerve conduction studies
findings.result: Symmetric sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy of the lower extremities.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Marked thrombocythemia: platelets 847 × 10^9/L; other routine values unremarkable.

findings.name: nailfold capillaroscopy
findings.result: Well-conserved capillaries with some giant loops and minor hemorrhages, consistent with early scleroderma.

findings.name: lumbar spine CT
findings.result: Degenerative changes and osteosclerotic lesions at L4–S1.

findings.name: MRI of the lumbar spine
findings.result: Lesions in the L5–S1 vertebrae with abnormal enhancement of the paraspinal muscles and subcutaneous tissue.

aliases: polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal gammopathy and skin changes syndrome
gold.reasoning: 1. Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy was considered given the demyelinating neuropathy — “diagnosis is often delayed with intervening incorrect diagnoses of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy…” 2. A myeloproliferative disorder (essential thrombocythemia) was considered due to striking thrombocythemia — “…‘triple negative’ essential thrombocythemia (based on bone marrow findings and absence of typical genetic features)…” and “myeloproliferative disorders are included in the differential diagnosis of POEMS syndrome.”

source_issues: s011: serum and urine immunofixation are repeatedly negative, although a monoclonal plasma cell disorder is a mandatory criterion of the gold diagnosis.
s007: 'anasarca of the lumbar region' mixes generalized and local edema.
s005: vital signs are reported without values.
notes: Index visit: the referral visit for possible systemic sclerosis (s001-s009); the laboratory tests, capillaroscopy, echocardiography, CT and MRI (s010-s016) are findings from the same staged workup.
s002 and s003: timing shared by several symptoms is written as standalone facts (f003, f007, f011).

Skin signs the patient can see (darkening, redness, mottling, thick tight skin, blue hands and feet, Raynaud's) are facts and stay in the skin examination; leukonychia, clubbing, jugular venous distention, edema, reflexes and papilledema are examiner findings only.
No VEGF level, bone marrow, endocrine testing or free light chains are reported; requests for them are unavailable.
